title: Terminal-Safe Nodes
statement: You are given a directed graph on n nodes labeled 0..n-1, described as an adjacency list graph where graph[i] is the list of nodes that node i points to. A node with no outgoing edges is called a terminal node. A node is safe when every path that starts at it is finite and eventually ends at a terminal node; equivalently, no path leaving the node can ever enter a cycle. Terminal nodes are themselves safe (the empty path already ends there). Return the labels of all safe nodes as a list sorted in strictly ascending order; return an empty list if no node is safe. If graph is empty, return an empty list.
hints: A node is doomed if any path from it can reach a cycle. Instead of chasing forward paths, ask: which nodes are guaranteed to bottom out at a dead end?

Flip every edge and run Kahn's peeling on the reversed graph, seeding the queue with the original graph's out-degree-zero nodes (the terminals); a node becomes safe only once all of its outgoing edges have been confirmed to lead to already-safe nodes.

Build reverse adjacency and an out_degree array for the original graph. Enqueue all nodes with out_degree 0 and mark them safe. Popping a node, walk its reverse edges and decrement each predecessor's out_degree; when a predecessor hits 0 it is safe, so enqueue it. Nodes trapped in or feeding a cycle never reach 0. Return the safe labels in ascending order.
